findings.evidence: The section states "This workspace holds 5 projects, synced last week." but the list below shows only 4 projects (Support Backlog Triage, Beta Launch Plan, Partner Integration Pilot, Mobile App Revamp).
findings.violation: The count and the displayed list do not match, creating confusion about the total number of projects.
findings.fix: Either add the fifth project to the visible list or change the count to match the number of displayed projects.

findings.evidence: The button is labeled "Save" with id="project-settings-save-btn"
findings.violation: The form uses "Save" as the button label, while the notification settings form (line 76) uses "Submit" for the same action type, creating inconsistent terminology.
findings.fix: Use consistent button labels across all forms in the interface; either standardize on "Save" or "Submit".

findings.violation: The button has only an aria-label with no visible text, making it inaccessible to users who do not use screen readers and making its purpose unclear from visual inspection alone.
findings.fix: Add visible button text or an icon with clear visual indication that this duplicates the project.

findings.location: Workspace overview section, recent projects list
findings.evidence:
• Support Backlog Triage
    • ...
  • Mobile App Revamp
with no heading indicating it is a "recent" list
findings.violation: The list context is unclear; users cannot distinguish whether this shows all projects, recent projects, or filtered projects, making it ambiguous what "recent" means.
findings.fix: Add a heading or label within the div with id="workspace-overview-recent" to clearly identify this as a "Recent projects" or "Recent activity" list.

findings.evidence: Archiving "Customer Migration" will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team. You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list.
findings.violation: The confirmation message assumes the user remembers which project they are about to archive, but users may have navigated away or forgotten context by the time they see this dialog.
findings.fix: Rephrase to be more explicit: "Are you sure you want to archive the project Customer Migration?"

findings.evidence: An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.
findings.violation: The message is vague about what the user should do next or whether there are further steps, and it does not confirm which email address was used.
findings.fix: Add clarity: "An invite has been sent to [email address]. The recipient has 5 days to accept. You can send additional invites or monitor acceptance in project settings."

findings.evidence: The last import finished with 3 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 63, 71, and 82 were skipped; every other row was imported.
findings.violation: The message only reports skipped rows but does not explain whether the import overall succeeded, failed, or partially succeeded, leaving ambiguity about the import status.
findings.fix: Prefix the message with a clear status indicator: "Import succeeded with warnings: 3 rows skipped..."

findings.evidence: <form><label for="notification-settings-digest-input">Digest frequency</label><select>...</select><button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Submit</button></form> with no cancel option
findings.violation: Users cannot cancel or revert changes after modifying the notification frequency, and there is no feedback about whether changes were saved.
findings.fix: Add a cancel button and a success confirmation message or indicator after submission.

findings.evidence: Multiple <a> links including "Go to notification settings", "Invite a team member", "Archive project", and "Back to your projects" mixed with form submission
findings.violation: The form and navigation links are not clearly separated visually or structurally, making it unclear which are form actions and which are navigation.
findings.fix: Group form actions together and separate navigation links into a distinct section or use consistent styling to differentiate them.

findings.location: Import status and workspace overview timing, line 11 and line 64
findings.evidence: Line 11: "synced last week", Line 64: "The last import finished..."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether "last week" refers to the same import event as "last import", creating ambiguity about data freshness and timing.
findings.fix: Align the timing language: use the same timestamp reference for both sections or make it explicit that they refer to different events.

findings.evidence: <input id="invite-member-email-input" type="email"> with no validation feedback or confirmation display
findings.violation: The form accepts an email input but provides no visual feedback about validation, confirmation of what will be sent, or error messages if validation fails.
findings.fix: Add a validation message and a confirmation step showing the email address before final submission.
